chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one in major ritual impurity (junub), when he wants to eat and drink, should wash his hand, rinse his mouth, wash his face, and then eat and drink.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The one in major ritual impurity (junub)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual purification steps for a junub before eating and drinking?
ai.summary: Reported through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir (AS), this hadith clarifies that a person in the state of *junub* (major impurity) is not required to perform full *ghusl* merely to eat or drink, but only needs to wash the hands, rinse the mouth, and wash the face. This ruling highlights the distinction between ritual purity for prayer and the practical hygiene required for daily sustenance, emphasizing ease in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one with sexual impurity, when he wants to eat and drink, should wash his hands, and he should rinse his mouth, and wash his face, and (then) eat and drink’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one after experiencing sexual relation likes to eat or drink, one must wash one’s hand, rinse one’s mouth, wash one’s face, then eat and drink.’”
